title: The page that shows what you pulled
summary: Pulling a card in TCG Card Shop Simulator does not only add stock: the game has a page of its own for a card you have obtained, with pages, a total value, a price graph and its own look for legend cards.
body: Pulling a card does not only add it to a shelf. The game keeps a page of its own for a card you have obtained, so what came out of a pack is presented as a result rather than only as stock.
That page counts as well as shows. It keeps a list of card amounts, a value group, a line for the value being shown and a total for everything in the result, so a pull can be judged in one place.
It is paged rather than scrolled. There are page texts, a value for the current page and next and previous buttons, which is how a large haul is read a screen at a time.
It can also show a price graph. The page carries the graph screen of its own, so a card can be weighed on how its price has moved rather than only on what it is worth right now.
Graded cards have a panel of their own. It can show the picture of an empty slot, a plus sign and the card itself with a value line, which is how a card and the case it went into are shown together.
Legend cards are not given a flat shine. Two materials are scrolled across the card at their own speeds on each axis, so the glow drifts instead of sitting still.
Collection packs have pictures of their own as well: a kind, a full picture, and a top and a bottom piece that can be used separately, so a pack can be shown whole or built from parts.
What this entry does not tell you: what any card is worth, how the glow is tuned, or how many collection packs there are. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game has a page of its own for a card you have obtained.
That page keeps a list of card amounts, a value group, a value line and a total value line.
The page has page texts and next and previous buttons.
The page carries the price graph screen of its own.
The graded card panel can show an empty slot picture, a plus sign, the card itself and a value line.
